transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. My kitchen table is completely covered—my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I started and never finished. And I sit there looking at it all, thinking I’ll start with one thing, but then I notice something else, and… oh, the church flyer had this luncheon on it I meant to ask someone about—anyway, by the time I try to decide what to do first, the whole day is gone. It’s gotten really frustrating.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay on task in other areas of your life, like when you're at church, volunteering, or talking with friends?

Yes, very much. At the senior center, if I’m trying to write down a note or plan something, and two people nearby start talking, my mind just goes right over to them. Or if the television is on in the next room, even softly, I’ll start listening to that without meaning to.

Then I look back down and I’ve completely lost where I was. I’ll think, “Now what was I writing?” It happens at church things too—well, like after service when everyone’s chatting and there are papers being handed around—I just can’t keep my mind on the one thing I meant to do.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, like you can't sit still for very long?

Yes… I do, though I wouldn’t say I’m up pacing all the time. It’s more when I’m supposed to be sitting still, like in a meeting or at church. I’ll be trying to look polite and listen, and then I realize I’m rubbing my hands together, or tapping my foot under the chair.

Sometimes I click my pen without noticing—oh, that drives people crazy, I know it does—and I’ll shift around so much that someone looks over at me. Then I get embarrassed and try to stop, but before long I’m doing something else with my hands again.
Do you ever find yourself interrupting others when they’re talking, or jumping into conversations or activities without being asked?

Hmm… I’m not sure about that one. I don’t think of myself as someone who barges in, at least not on purpose. I mean, sometimes in a group I’ll start to say something because I’m afraid I’ll forget it, and then I realize someone else wasn’t quite finished—but then again, everyone sort of talks over each other after church coffee, you know? Especially when they’re passing around the cookies and someone’s asking about the flower committee—oh, I used to help with that, and the sign-up sheets were always such a mess.

But… no, I don’t really know if I interrupt more than other people. I haven’t noticed it as a big problem, I guess.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like church activities or time with friends?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I still go to church things when I remember what’s happening—well, when I remember to look at the bulletin, I should say. And I do like seeing people there, especially after service when everyone stands around with coffee, though sometimes it gets noisy and I lose track of who I was talking to.

As far as feeling down… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that exactly. Some days I get frustrated with myself, but that’s not quite the same thing, is it? I still enjoy people, I think. I just—sorry, what part were you asking again?
Have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like volunteering or spending time with friends, even if you still participate in them?

I’m not sure I’d say I no longer take pleasure in them. I still like being around people, I think. Volunteering… well, I haven’t done as much of that lately, but some of that is just the way things get organized, and then someone changes the time, and the bulletin says one thing and the email says another—at least, that happened once with the luncheon committee, and everyone was confused.

But no, I don’t think I’ve noticed that I don’t enjoy things anymore. I might feel sort of worn out or scattered when I’m there, but if I’m with friends or at church, I usually do feel glad I went. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often feel worried or on edge, especially when you're trying to focus or organize things?

I’m not sure I’d call it worried or on edge exactly. I mean, when I’m trying to organize papers or get something ready, I can get… well, bothered, I suppose, if things aren’t where I thought they were. But then sometimes I find the thing in a perfectly obvious place, like next to the telephone, which reminds me I still haven’t sorted that little basket by the phone with the church notes and coupons in it.

But anxious—do you mean like nervous? I don’t know that I’ve noticed that as a main thing. I mostly just get a little flustered sometimes, but I wouldn’t know if that’s what you mean.
Would you say that, even when you're with friends or at church, you don't enjoy those moments as much as you used to, or feel like you're just going through the motions?

I don’t think I’d put it that way, no. I mean, sometimes during church I’m thinking about whether I put the kettle on before I left, or if I remembered to bring back that casserole dish to Carol—well, not casserole, it was more of a serving bowl—but when I’m actually talking with people, I think I do enjoy it.

“Going through the motions”… I’m not sure. I still like being there. I may not always follow everything the way I should, especially if there are announcements and then someone asks me something right after, but I don’t think it feels empty or anything like that. At least, I haven’t noticed that.
Have you, in the past two weeks, felt like nothing really brings you pleasure or that you can’t get interested in things, even things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think I can say that nothing brings me pleasure, no. I mean, I still get interested in things, at least if I can get myself to sit with them long enough. Sometimes I’ll start reading the church newsletter and then notice the plant by the window needs water, and then I’m in the kitchen wondering why I went in there—so it may look like I’m not interested, but I don’t know that it feels that way inside.

The past two weeks… I’m trying to think. I’ve still enjoyed little things. Talking to people, being out when I get there. So no, I haven’t really noticed a “nothing feels good” kind of thing.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are slowed down or foggy, like it’s harder to think clearly or make decisions than it used to be?

Foggy… hmm. I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say my thoughts feel slowed down exactly, not like walking through mud or anything. Sometimes I do stand in the kitchen thinking, “Now what was I deciding?” but then there’s usually the mail on the counter, and I remember I meant to call someone, or check whether the milk was still good.

As for making decisions, well, little things can take me a while—like which card to send someone, and then I start looking through the drawer and find old stamps. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean by foggy. I haven’t really thought of it as my mind being slowed down.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or like you don’t have much energy lately, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Tired… I’m trying to think. I mean, I’m 70, so some days I sit down after lunch and think, “Well, that chair is awfully comfortable,” but I don’t know if that’s unusual. And sometimes I’ll start to do something simple, like fold towels, and then I notice one of them has a loose thread, which reminds me I meant to look for the sewing kit—though I think it’s in the hallway closet, unless I moved it when my niece came over.

But energy-wise… I’m not sure I’ve noticed a big change lately. I do get tired here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling drained for no reason. At least not that I can clearly point to.

When you're in situations where you're expected to sit still for a while, like during a church service or a doctor’s appointment, do you often feel like you can't stay seated or need to move, even if you try to stay calm?

Yes… I think so. Not so much that I feel panicky or anything, but I do seem to get up a lot when I’m supposed to just sit and listen.

Like at volunteer meetings, I’ll suddenly think, “Oh, I should check the calendar,” or I’ll need to find a paper in my bag, or I’ll get up to refill my water. And even at supper, I’ll pop up to get something or look for something, then I’m halfway across the room before I remember everyone else is still sitting there. It’s not always because I truly need to, I just… don’t stay put very well.
Have you had trouble with focus or staying organized for most of your life, even when you were younger—like when you were working or raising your family?

Yes, I suppose it does go way back. I was just thinking about this little blue report card my mother kept in a drawer with old birthday cards—she saved everything, even receipts from the hardware store for some reason.

But yes, even when I was a little girl, the teachers would write things like, “bright, but careless,” which I hated seeing. I’d forget my books or my homework, or I’d have to be reminded to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. I remember everyone else lining up for recess, and I’d still be at my desk trying to finish something I should’ve done already. So, yes, it’s not really new.
